assessment: Mana binds this deck, not power: 34 land copies against the 36-38 band, 28 of 66 nonland entries at mana value five or more, and land drops falling to 60.3% on turn five and 49.7% on turn six. Six of the ten buy mana or buy discount. Three answer the fact that every infinite in the 99 routes through one enchantment — the corpus's prescription for a linear deck is 'redundancy that shrugs off three answers' (strategy:critical-mass), and the extra-combat ignition currently assembles 6.4%, 3.6% by turn six. The tenth covers the graveyard, the only permanent class the deck answers with nothing. No pick moves the computed bracket floor off 4.

ten.why: Two mana off one land is the only pool card that moves the number the audit blames — mean available mana 4.937 on turn six against a 28-card shelf at mana value five or more — and it turns turn five into an Old Gnawbone turn instead of a Farseek turn.
ten.unlocks: The deck's 5-to-9 drops start arriving on the turn the plan wants them rather than two turns late; the mana is unrestricted, so it also pays Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R}.

ten.why: One red mana finds Aggravated Assault, which six of the deck's seven tutors cannot: Encroaching Dragonstorm and Skyshroud Claim fetch lands, Nature's Lore a Forest, Sarkhan's Triumph a Dragon creature, Worldly Tutor any creature, Tiamat Dragon cards — only Enlightened Tutor reaches an enchantment.
ten.unlocks: A named one-of stops being 7.1% of an opening seven; on a stalled turn six the same card fetches the land instead. The random discard is the price — cast it with cards in hand, not on an empty one, because Haven of the Spirit Dragon and Rivaz of the Claw only bring back Dragons.

ten.why: An untapped source of all five colours in a deck holding red at 27 sources against a 36 target while red carries 47 of 101 pips, and where The Ur-Dragon and Tiamat each want all five colours in one cost.
ten.unlocks: A land that is never the reason a turn-five Dragon sits in hand. The life beside City of Brass is real; the deck's turn-five and turn-six problem is land drops at 0.603 and 0.497, not life total.

ten.why: The second extra-combat effect the 99 does not have, and it is a Dragon: eminence and the three cost reducers cut its cast, and Sarkhan's Triumph, Worldly Tutor and Tiamat can all go get it.
ten.unlocks: One Disenchant no longer ends the combo plan. The honest price is the activation — {5}{R}{R} against Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R}, so Old Gnawbone's Treasures are the funding, exactly as in the certified Gnawbone loop.

ten.closes: engine component: cost reducers (Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn, Dragonspeaker Shaman)
ten.why: The deck's declared curve fixer is three cards — 19.9% of openers, 42.3% measured — and this is a fourth that covers red, which sits on 32 of the deck's cards including the commander's own generic cost.
ten.unlocks: A discount that Crux of Fate's non-Dragon mode and Dragonback Assault's 3 damage cannot switch off, unlike Dragonspeaker Shaman at 2/2. The cut is priced painful and it is spent deliberately: an eight-mana enchantment no discount reaches, for a two-mana discount that reaches 32 cards.

ten.why: A repeatable extra combat that is not an enchantment, so the answer that kills Aggravated Assault does not kill this too — and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} is a cost a five-colour deck already making Treasures off Old Gnawbone, Goldspan Dragon, Atsushi and Cavern-Hoard Dragon can actually pay.
ten.unlocks: A second ignition at three mana instead of three-plus-five, and Treasure mana is legal for an activated ability where Klauth's and Unclaimed Territory's is not. It is a 3/2 non-Dragon: your own Crux of Fate non-Dragon mode and Dragonback Assault both kill it.

ten.why: The obsolescence index lists it against Skyshroud Claim at similarity 0.9936 on lower mana value, and on turn two it fetches Stomping Ground, Breeding Pool or Overgrown Tomb — untapped for two life — rather than waiting until turn four for two Forest cards.
ten.unlocks: A third copy of the Farseek / Nature's Lore effect at the turn the deck can still afford it, which is where the land-drop curve breaks rather than where it starts.

ten.why: A 35th land that is also the deck's first answer to an opposing graveyard: nothing in the 99 touches one, so a reanimator seat is currently beaten on speed or on the stack or not at all.
ten.unlocks: A land drop and a graveyard exile in the same slot, and a black source where black sits at 16. Read the measure honestly: card_roles gives this card land:tapped only, so a re-run of the audit will still report the graveyard class uncovered — the card answers it on the battlefield, the taxonomy cannot see it.

ten.closes: engine component: cost reducers (Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn, Dragonspeaker Shaman)
ten.why: Three mana discounts every Dragon spell including the commander, and its 2/4 body survives Dragonback Assault's 3 damage where Dragonspeaker Shaman at 2/2 and Rivaz of the Claw at 3/3 both die.
ten.unlocks: Beside Ruby Medallion the reducer group goes from three cards to five, which the corpus prices at 31% of openers against the 19.9% three buys. The copy trigger is the upside: on the turn Old Gnawbone lands you get a second Treasure engine, and Sarkhan is a Dragon while the copy lasts, so Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas count it.

ten.why: One mana, and it is the only pick that moves the axis: running deck_audit's breadth function over the 99 with this card added takes graveyard from 0 answers to 1 and the class count from 4 to 5.
ten.unlocks: An entry-trigger exile against the reanimator's target, a sacrifice that exiles every opponent's graveyard before their turn, and a card if neither matters. Small, cheap, and the class it covers is the one the deck currently has no card for at all.

gaps: Every combo line above is unverified. Two are worth a stack scenario, in order: Old Gnawbone + Hellkite Charger, where the combo record itself lists mana_value_needed 7 and the question is whether one connection's Treasures cover the next activation the way they do for Aggravated Assault; and Najeela, the Blade-Blossom + Old Gnawbone, where the question is whether a Treasure-funded {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} sustains across combats when black sits at 16 sources.

The funding family did not make the ten and the reason is the same for all of it. The Reaver Cleaver opens the most popular Aggravated Assault line in the database (34,407) and Sword of Feast and Famine and Bear Umbra both untap lands to pay for the next activation — but none of them makes Aggravated Assault replaceable, which is the hole. Helm of the Host with Scourge of the Throne is the one line that skips Assault entirely; it costs 4 to cast plus 5 to equip against mean available mana of 4.937 on turn six, so the binding axis prices it out before its rules question is even asked.

Ancient Silver Dragon is named by the pilot and stays off. It is an eight-drop in the deck whose measured weakness is a five-plus shelf 28 entries deep, and the card-advantage count reads low mostly because the taxonomy cannot see Dragon's Hoard, Return of the Wildspeaker, Rishkar's Expertise, Tiamat or the commander's attack trigger — a probe note, not a hole. Sneak Attack does cheat it in for {R} (verified, stack 005), so the case is real; overriding the curve here is a pilot call and not a data one. Hellkite Tyrant and Faeburrow Elder return nothing in any evidence channel: Tyrant's theft line is live in Treasure pods, and Faeburrow's {W} pip sits on the deck's thinnest colour at 15 sources.

No pick carries a synergy claim. The synergy graph's shortlists for these ten return generic Ramp + Cost Reduction pairings scored 1 against in-deck rocks and lands, which is the format-wide top-10 doing its job and not a statement about this list.

goldfish_targets.json declares components by card name, so a swap silently shrinks one until the declaration is re-run: the ramp group names Skyshroud Claim, and the reducer group holds three cards that Ruby Medallion and Sarkhan, Soul Aflame do not join by themselves. Any measured rate quoted here is the rate for the declared cards, not for the deck after a swap.
